To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a simple empirical regression can be used to predict total P reduction by a VFS based on the hydrological (infiltration rate) and sedimentological (sediment reduction) response of the VFS.

the infiltration and sedimentation by the filter strip are the primary factors controlling total phosphorus (P), and a predictive equation for P reduction by vegetative filter strips (based on the hydrologic response of the filter strip) can be developed using a multiple linear regression approach.
a simple empirical regression equation can be derived to predict total phosphorus trapping efficiency of a vegetative filter based on the physical response of infiltration and sedimentation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an empirical equation for quantifying total P reduction by a VFS based on runoff reduction and sediment reduction.
the development of a simple empirical model for quantifying total phosphorus reduction by vegetative filter strips.
the development of a simple empirical model that can be used for the design or evaluation (assessment) of VFS for total P removal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a simple regression model can predict total P trapping efficiency based on infiltration and sediment trapping efficiency.

a multiple linear regression model for predicting total P reduction in a vegetative filter strips is possible and can be improved if the initial P concentration in the VFS and sediment reduction is considered.
the proposed empirical model is a simple, practical, and reliable tool to estimate total P trapping efficiencies by VFS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed regression model is useful in the design or assessment of water quality improvements of early stage VFS where the soil P is not saturated and the P associated with sediment is not accumulated in the filter.
a regression model was developed to predict total P reduction by VFS based on the infiltration and sedimentation response of the filter.
we have developed an empirical model for predicting total P trapping efficiency of vegetative filter strips that is based on infiltration and sediment reduction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the empirical model developed here provides a simple and effective means to quantify P removal by VFS and to assess their potential to reduce P concentrations in receiving waters.
the proposed model provides a simple and practical approach for estimating the reduction in total P concentration by a vegetative buffer.
the empirical model for quantifying total P reduction by vegetative filter strips developed in our research can be used in design or evaluation of VFS in the early stage of development.
